question_type: Cubic polynomial extrapolation of a 25-year annual surplus/deficit series stitched across 5-year FFO-1 windows, compared with the Treasury's printed estimate for 2025

opus_path.decision: 25 annual points 1989-2013, degree-3 least squares in year, extrapolate to 2025, absolute difference vs the Treasury's 2025 estimate; flagged 'calendar years' vs the Bulletin's fiscal-year tables as an ambiguity to resolve.

Located the comparator as the FFO-1 'Summary of Fiscal Operations' row '2025 - Est', Total surplus/deficit column; listed all three published vintages of that estimate and chose the latest, most-repeated one (4 latest issues).
FFO-1 prints only 5 fiscal years per issue, so the 1989-2013 series must be stitched across issues.

Wrote extract_ffo1.py to scan every issue >= 1989 for FFO-1 (OCR-tolerant title regex), find the 'Total surplus' column by header, and collect every printing of every year row; separated stable years from revised years (1989, 1999-2005, 2007).
Row-level check receipts - outlays = surplus for every chosen row; fixed a title-regex miss and discarded continuation-table stray values.
Vintage rule: latest printing of each fiscal year (September issue of FY+5); alternatives (block-Sep, block-Dec, first-published) computed and recorded.
Calendar vs fiscal: only FFO-1 has both the 1989-2013 totals and a 2025 estimate, there is no calendar-year 2025 estimate, so the FFO-1 year rows are the intended 'years'.
Exact rational least squares on centered x, numpy cross-check; calc.py re-reads and asserts all 25 cited lines.
Magnitude sanity and sensitivity: data-vintage choice moves the answer by ~0.2%, first-published data by ~5%, comparator vintage by 10-20%.

opus_key_moves: Resolved 'calendar years' by asking where both the historical series AND the comparator exist (only FFO-1 year rows), instead of reconstructing calendar sums
Collected every printing of every year row with a chronologically ordered, header-aware extractor, then took the latest printing per year and verified each row arithmetically
Used exact arithmetic (centered x, rational normal equations) and printed alternatives for every open choice

first_divergence.what_glm_did: Took 'calendar years' literally and decided to build each year's total by summing monthly FFO-1 rows from that year's December issue ([28]); dismissed the FFO-1 annual rows it saw at [19]-[20] because they are fiscal years.
first_divergence.what_opus_did: Used the printed FFO-1 annual (fiscal-year) rows, stitched across issues at their latest printing, reasoning that only FFO-1 has both the series and the 2025 estimate.
first_divergence.why_glm_went_that_way: [22] 'Question says reported total surplus/deficit values from calendar years 1989-2013 ... Calendar year values can be summed monthly'; [28] 'For calendar year 1989, Dec 1989 bulletin includes Jan-Dec 1989. Great.'
first_divergence.consequence: Its 25 inputs are a derived monthly-sum series rather than the printed annual rows; the cubic extrapolation amplifies the differences and the final is ~38% above the accepted answer.

secondary_errors.note: Date-window misread: a December issue's monthly block runs September of the prior year through September of the current year (e.g. 1989_12.txt:669-681, 2005_12.txt:610-622), so its 'first Oct/Nov/Dec rows' were the previous year's months. Where the block starts with a year-labeled September, the code actually summed Oct(y-1)..Sep(y), i.e. a fiscal year from first printings, while the actor believed it had calendar years.

Label matching on bare month names: in 1989_12 the block's first row is an unlabeled 'Sept' (1988) at line 669, so the code's 'first Sept' precedes '1989 - Jan' and the Jan..Sept slice is empty - the 1989 'total' is only Jan 1989 plus Oct-Dec 1988. It also used a fixed column index r[7] with no header check. Several years deviate by >50% from the printed annual row (1989, 1999-2001) while others match within 1%; no per-year check against printed totals.

Its only series validation was recall-based ('known calendar year deficits ... plausible'); at [56] it explicitly asked whether Oct-Dec came from the prior year and reassured itself they were 1989's, and it accepted a 1989 total less than half the printed FY1989 row as a plausible calendar-year figure. The fit arithmetic itself was re-checked by hand at [56] and was consistent.

saw_correct_evidence.where: [19]-[20] saw FFO-1 annual rows (2009-2013) in 2014_03; [24] saw the correct '2025 - Est' comparator (which it used). Never collected the annual rows for 1989-2008.

remedies.intervention: Derived-series sanity check: when an annual value is reconstructed from monthly cells, compare it with any printed annual total for the same or overlapping period and flag large deviations; also require the parser to locate the target column by header text.
remedies.why: The printed FFO-1 annual rows were one read away; >50% mismatches in several years would have exposed both the window misread and the column misparse.

remedies.intervention: Table extractor that returns a clean grid with header-resolved column names and fully qualified period keys for monthly rows (fill the year down from 'YYYY - Mon' anchors).
remedies.why: Both secondary errors (wrong-year Oct-Dec rows; fixed r[7] index) are parsing errors a structured extractor removes.

remedies.intervention: Lesson: Treasury Bulletin FFO-1 annual rows are fiscal years; questions saying 'calendar years' about FFO-1 totals and an FFO-1 estimate usually mean these year rows; use the latest printing per year.
remedies.why: Plausible from Opus's reasoning, but the question is on the disputed list (issue47) and the literal reading is defensible, so the lesson is benchmark-convention knowledge rather than a reading rule.

right_arms_note: No GLM arm was right. The prompt arm matched Opus's interpretation, table, comparator and fit and missed only through stale vintages for seven revised years after state loss; none and cards took 'calendar years' literally and built monthly-sum series.
text_vs_mechanism: Mechanism. The prompt arm had and initially applied the relevant vintage text, then lost the correct state through compactions and reintroduced an unsorted-glob bug that its circular check could not catch - that needs STATE persistence plus an all-printings tool/check. For none/cards the calendar-vs-fiscal choice is a genuine ambiguity (issue47) that text could bias, but a two-reading fork with a tiebreak rule is more reliable than a phrasing lesson.
notes: issue47 = true: the question is disputed and the calendar/fiscal wording is literally inconsistent with the only table carrying a 2025 estimate. Sensitivity (from Opus): comparator vintage dominates (10-20%), then first-published vs revised data (~5%), then revised-vintage choice (~0.2%) - so a harness should surface the comparator-row choice first. Loop-plus-compaction behavior in both long arms (prompt, cards) is a harness-level failure independent of the question.
